issues.legal_issue: Acceptance of rent paid before a lease expires does not, without assent to continued possession after expiry, create a holding over under section 116 of the Transfer of Property Act.
material_facts: The lease was treated by both sides as expiring on a fixed date, and their correspondence reflected an expectation that the lessee would hand over possession then.
Rent covering a period extending beyond the stated expiry was paid and accepted before that expiry, rather than after it.
The correspondence did not show that the lessor assented to the lessee continuing in possession after the lease expired.
At most, the parties’ financial-year practice supported treating the lease period as extended to the end of that financial year.
issues.conclusion: There was no holding over under section 116. Even if the lease period was treated as extended to the end of the financial year, it then expired and the lessor was entitled to possession without notice under section 106.
issues.legal_principle: Section 116 of the Transfer of Property Act requires the lessee to remain in possession after determination of the lease and the lessor to accept rent or otherwise assent to continued possession. Acceptance of rent is relevant only when made at a time and in a manner equivalent to assent to continued possession; payment made before expiry, when neither party treated it as assent, does not suffice. K. B. Capadia v. Bai Jerbai Warden and Another, where rent was accepted after the tenancy expired, was distinguished. On the alternative view that the lease was extended to the end of the financial year, it expired then and no notice under section 106 was necessary before re-entry.

predicates.lease_possession_dispute: The dispute concerns a lessor seeking possession after a lease has ended.
predicates.rent_paid_before_lease_termination: The lessee paid, and the lessor accepted, rent for a period extending beyond the stated expiry before that expiry occurred.
predicates.parties_treated_lease_as_ending_on_a_fix: The parties’ conduct and communications treated the lease as ending on a fixed date rather than continuing thereafter.
predicates.no_lessor_assent_to_post_expiry_possessi: The lessor did not assent to the lessee continuing in possession after the lease ended.

issues.definition: When a possession dispute involves rent paid before the lease ends, the parties treat the lease as ending on a fixed date, and the lessor does not assent to occupation afterward, the result is no statutory holding over.

issues.legal_issue: A lease clause allowing specified materials to remain after expiry transfers only manufactured building materials left beyond the permitted period, not machinery, equipment, or plant.
material_facts: The lease allowed the lessee to keep bricks, boilers, engines, trucks, kilns, railway and tram lines, and other materials on the premises for three months after expiry.
A separate clause addressed early termination for breach and required removal of boilers, engines, trucks, kilns, railway and tram lines, and other materials.
The lease expired in the ordinary way, and bricks and other manufactured materials remained on the premises beyond the permitted period.
The lessee’s boilers, engines, trucks, kilns, railway and tram lines, and similar plant were distinct from building materials such as bricks and tiles.
issues.conclusion: The lessor acquired only the building materials, such as bricks, tiles, and similar articles manufactured on the premises. The lessee was allowed time from the decree to remove the boilers, engines, trucks, kilns, railway and tram lines, and similar items.
issues.legal_principle: The lease must be construed as a whole. The early-termination clause applied when the lessor terminated for breach and did not govern expiry by efflux of time. The clause governing ordinary expiry made building materials left in contravention of its removal period the lessor’s property; “other materials” in that context referred to building materials, not machinery, tools, or plant.

predicates.lease_expiry_dispute: The dispute concerns ownership or removal of items left on leased premises when the lease ends.
predicates.lease_expired_by_efflux_of_time: The lease ended through the ordinary expiry of its term rather than early termination for breach.
predicates.manufactured_building_materials_left_bey: The lessee left building materials manufactured on the premises beyond the period allowed for their removal.

issues.definition: When a lease ends by ordinary expiry and manufactured building materials remain beyond the permitted removal period, the lessor owns those materials but not the lessee’s plant or machinery.

issues.legal_issue: A lessor established to own materials left on leased premises may obtain an injunction restraining their removal or disposal even if the lessor is not in possession of them.
material_facts: The lessor sought an injunction to prevent the lessees from removing or disposing of the materials left on the premises.
The court found that the building materials left beyond the permitted period had become the lessor’s property.
The lessees argued that the lessor could not obtain an injunction without seeking a declaration of title and possession over the materials.
issues.conclusion: The injunction could be granted because the lessor’s ownership of the materials had been established; there was no legal objection to the relief sought.
issues.legal_principle: Where the claimant’s title to the property is established, there is no legal objection to an injunction restraining its removal or disposal. Ratnasabhapathi Pillai v. Ramaswami Aiyar, Bhramar Lal Banduri v. Nanda Lal Chowdhuri, and Valia Tamburatti v. Parvati were considered inapplicable to the circumstances.

predicates.property_injunction_dispute: The dispute concerns a request to restrain removal or disposal of property.
predicates.claimant_ownership_established: The claimant has established ownership of the property at issue.
predicates.removal_or_disposal_is_sought_to_be_rest: The claimant seeks to prevent another person from removing or disposing of the property.

issues.definition: When ownership is established in a property dispute and removal or disposal is sought to be restrained, an injunction may be granted.
